reference.title: Side Lunge
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step out and sit back, exhale as you push back to the middle.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s out and down, short pause, about 1.4 s back

prescription.progression: Hold a dumbbell at the chest (goblet lateral lunge)

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, arms forward.
Take a wide step to the side, toes pointing forward or slightly out.
Breathe in and sit the hips back over the stepping foot; keep the other leg straight and both heels down.
Breathe out and push off the stepping foot back to the middle.
Stand tall and reset; alternate sides.

mistakes.mistake: Knee caving in past the toes
mistakes.fix: Push the knee out in line with the stepping foot.

mistakes.mistake: Heel of the stepping foot lifting
mistakes.fix: Sit the hips back rather than down; reduce depth.
Hinge at the hips with the chest up.

kinematics.peak: 79 cm between ankle centres (about one leg length, shorter than the 60%-of-height standard in Riemann 2013)
kinematics.norm: Standardised lateral step of 60% of body height tested (Riemann 2013); self-selected steps were similar
About 80-90 degrees; knee flexion was about 13% lower than in forward lunges (Riemann 2013)

kinematics.peak: Step out 0.6 s, 1.2 s down, 0.3 s pause, 0.85 s up, step in 0.65 s

sources.title: Riemann et al. 2013, biomechanical comparison of forward and lateral lunges at varying step lengths (J Sports Med Phys Fitness 53:130-138)
Escamilla et al. 2008, patellofemoral compressive force and stress during forward and side lunges with and without a stride (Clin Biomech 23:1026-1037)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Patellofemoral stress was higher in the side lunge than the forward lunge at 80-90 degrees of knee flexion (Escamilla 2008): people with kneecap pain can use a shallower depth.
modify: Groin strain history: smaller step and less depth.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Stepping-leg knee extensors control the sit and drive the push back. Knee and ankle impulses were greater in lateral than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Stepping-leg knee extensors control the sit and drive the push back. Knee and ankle impulses were greater in lateral than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; works hardest out of the bottom. Longer steps raised gluteus maximus activity more than knee-extensor activity (Song 2023).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; works hardest out of the bottom. Longer steps raised gluteus maximus activity more than knee-extensor activity (Song 2023).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Both sides work: the stepping leg controls the wide position, the straight leg is stretched along its inner thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Both sides work: the stepping leg controls the wide position, the straight leg is stretched along its inner thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Lateral lunges asked more of the ankle than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Lateral lunges asked more of the ankle than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall and the pelvis level.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).

guides.label: Hips sit back over the foot
